text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall (severity=sev2) - sustained p95 latency spike for text-generation API across us-west-1 clusters. Alert: p95 > 3000ms for 5m. Links: https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/ALERT-745

erika: I’m on it. seeing a big P95 jump starting ~10:32 UTC, p50 up ~20% but p95 doubled. Any customer 1st reports?

mike: Customer support says a few high-volume customers noticed slow responses since 10:30. No widespread 5xx. Mostly latency.

erika: ack. grabbing traces and perf counters. josh, can you start handoff if this stays live?

josh: i'll standby for handoff. setting status page draft: "Increased API latency in us-west; investigating."

tracing-bot: New trace collection started for service=redwood-runtime, sampling=100% (ephemeral pull for incident). Trace bucket: gs://traces/incident-1759008765/

erika: past deploys? infra-bot, any kernel or node-level changes in last hour?

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: no model runtime deploys in last 2h. Node maintenance: kernel rollforward to 6.1.21 on a subset of pool-usw1-k3 at 09:50 UTC (30% of nodes).

erika: okay that's a good lead. hypothesis 1: kernel change affecting scheduler/steal causing longer tail. hypothesis 2: workload mix changed -> longer sequences -> MV batch fragmentation. We'll triage both.

mike: can we confirm request size/seq length distribution? I can dump recent request headers.

erika: please do. also capture /metrics from runtime pods and dmesg from nodes with new kernel.

mike: pasted sample counts (10:25-10:35): seq_len<=128: 60%, 128-512: 30%, >512:10%. Not a big change vs baseline.

erika: okay not sequence shift. josh: can you run perf counters on a new-kernel node and an old-kernel node, same service? Steps: ssh node, sudo perf stat -a -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,cycles,instructions sleep 30.

josh: running now on node-k3-07 (new kernel) and node-k2-04 (old). will post results.

josh: node-k3-07 perf: context-switches 1.8M, cpu-migrations 40k, cycles 45B, instructions 38B.
josh: node-k2-04 perf: context-switches 800k, cpu-migrations 12k, cycles 30B, instructions 26B.

erika: wow context switches ~2x on new-kernel nodes. That lines up with scheduler churn. keeps CPU bound but higher overhead.

mike: any cgroups/irq affinity changes? infra-bot?

infra-bot: No cgroup config changes. IRQ affinity consistent. Kernel patch notes show a scheduler backport in 6.1.21 that adjusted load-balancing heuristics.

erika: mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel on a subset (slow). 2) move traffic away from new-kernel nodes (quick). 3) enable tighter cpu-pin / isolcpus for runtime pods (medium). 4) fallback to smaller model for heavy customers (app-level). Which is fastest?

josh: we can cordon new-kernel nodes and drain new requests within ~5-7m. I'd prefer selective traffic shift to avoid mass drain.

mike: will contact traffic-router to shift weights off pool-usw1-k3 to k2 for text-gen route. ETA 4m.

erika: do it. while that ramps, enable aggressive KV prefix caching for long tails to reduce token generation per request. rollout config snippet:

erika: ```
route: /v1/generate
kv_cache: {
  prefix_cache: true,
  max_prefix_tokens: 256
}
```

erika: ops: rolling traffic shift started at 10:40 UTC.

tracing-bot: Trace diff (10:25-10:35 vs 10:40-10:50) uploaded: gs://traces/incident-1759008765/diff.json

mike: after shift p50 back to baseline, p95 dropped from ~3200ms to ~900ms in 6m window. Support reporting partial customer relief.

erika: great. still need to confirm root cause. josh, can you attach dmesg excerpts from a new-kernel node and old-kernel node?

josh: new-kernel dmesg shows repeated preempt_warning and rq balancing logs: "sched: RT throttling disabled" and frequent "softirq raise" messages. Old-kernel quiet.

erika: collecting kernel perf top and scheduler trace. Also getting runtime logs for get_worker_queue latency.

mike: runtime logs showing increased latency in accept loop and coroutine scheduling. snippet:

mike: ```
[10:33:05] INFO handle_request id=abc gen_time=2.1s
[10:33:06] WARN schedule_wait=1200us cpu_yield=800us
[10:33:07] INFO kv_lookup=100us gen_token_time=1.9s
```

erika: hypothesis refined: kernel scheduler changes increase context-switch frequency leading to higher scheduler wake latencies -> runtime coroutine scheduling overhead -> p95 spike. Primary repro signal: perf counts + dmesg + trace spans showing waiting'desched' steps. Hypothesis 2 (model/sequence) deprioritized.

josh: next steps: open ticket with infra to revert kernel on affected nodes or pin traffic to old pool until we verify kernel patch. Also create perf regression ticket for kernel 6.1.21.

infra-bot: Reversion plan: schedule rollback for pool-usw1-k3 tonight, immediate option: cordon and move traffic off.

erika: for customer comms: we observed increased p95 starting 10:32 UTC after partial kernel roll; we mitigated by shifting traffic and enabling caching at 10:40 UTC. Impact: elevated latency for ~8 minutes for a subset of customers; no request errors.

mike: added list of affected customers (support ticket IDs): #SUP-4541, #SUP-4542, #SUP-4548.

erika: creating incident timeline and RCA doc. Everyone add traces/log excerpts to the shared doc: https://wiki.redwood.example/incidents/1759008765-rca (please paste selected logs, perf outputs).

josh: putting perf outputs and dmesg into the doc. Also adding command snippets used for repro.

josh: repro guidance: to reproduce load run the benchmark harness with 100 concurrent clients and sequence lengths 256+, monitor perf stat on nodes with kernel 6.1.21. We saw CLUSTER p95 > 2x baseline.

erika: thanks. final immediate action: keep pool-usw1-k3 cordoned; infra to rollback during maintenance window or repro kernel patch upstream. Ops: postmortem owners: erika (lead), josh (kernel traces), mike (customer comms).

mike: drafting postmortem now. will include timeline, perf counters, traces, mitigations, and recommended follow-ups: revert kernel, add perf counters alerting for context-switch spikes, and traffic-aware deploy policy.

erika: closing live coordination. If new uptick occurs re-open page. Great work team :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident updated: severity=sev2 -> mitigation_in_place. Incident channel will be archived when RCA doc published.
